title: Learning with AI: shortcut or study partner?
titleDe: Lernen mit KI – Abkürzung oder Lernhilfe?

task.situation: ‘Brainwave’, an online magazine written by and for young people, is planning an issue on learning in the digital age. The editors have invited readers to send in articles on the question ‘Learning with AI: shortcut or study partner?’ A selection will appear on the magazine’s website next month.
task.instruction: Write an article in which you:
points: describe how AI tools can help students with their learning
explain the risks of relying on AI for schoolwork
suggest rules for using AI in a way that supports learning

words.short: Give your article a title. Write around 250 words.
words.long: Give your article a title. Write around 400 words.

task.de: Ein Artikel für ein Online-Jugendmagazin über KI beim Lernen. Drei Inhaltspunkte: beschreiben, wie KI-Werkzeuge beim Lernen helfen können; die Risiken erklären; Regeln für einen sinnvollen Umgang vorschlagen. Zuerst wählt ihr die Grundhaltung, der Titel kommt ganz zum Schluss.

meta.publication: Brainwave · online magazine by and for young people

focus.label: hedging
focus.note: Marked: hedging, i.e. words that make a claim more careful: may, might, tend to, be likely / unlikely to, seem to, probably. ‘Can’ (ability) and frequency words such as ‘often’ are not marked.

gaps.q: Who do we quote? Give the student a first name.
gaps.qDe: Ruft einen Vornamen für die Person, die wir zitieren. Keine Namen von Mitschüler:innen oder Lehrer:innen.

steps.q: Shortcut or study partner? Which view does our article take?
steps.de: Zuerst wählt ihr die Grundhaltung des Artikels; sie bestimmt Einstieg, Schluss und einen der Titel.

options.label: Mainly a study partner
options.teaser: AI can be a real help for learning, as long as students follow a few rules.

options.label: Mainly a risky shortcut
options.teaser: AI tempts students to skip the learning, so they should use it rarely and with care.

steps.q: How do we open the article?
steps.de: Der erste Absatz soll Leser:innen neugierig machen und zur Frage des Artikels führen. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then finish the introduction in your own words and make clear which view the article takes.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann den Einstieg mit eigenen Worten fertigschreiben; die Grundhaltung soll erkennbar sein.

options.label: Start with a scene

map.partner: {{It is late on a Sunday evening,}} and tomorrow’s chemistry test is getting closer. {{Instead of texting a friend, many students}} now ask an AI chatbot to explain the topic. Is this a clever shortcut or a bad habit? {{Used wisely, the chatbot [[may]] be}} a better study partner than many people think.
map.shortcut: {{It is late on a Sunday evening,}} and tomorrow’s chemistry test is getting closer. {{Instead of texting a friend, many students}} now ask an AI chatbot to explain the topic. Is this a clever shortcut or a bad habit? {{Convenient as it is, this kind of help [[may]]}} cost more than it saves.

options.why: A short scene that many readers know from their own lives leads straight to the question.

options.label: Speak to the readers

map.partner: {{Be honest: when did you last ask an AI tool for homework help?}} If the answer is ‘yesterday’, you are in good company, as chatbots are now part of everyday school life. {{The real question is how we use them:}} as a shortcut that skips learning or as a partner that [[might]] make it easier.
map.shortcut: {{Be honest: when did you last ask an AI tool for homework help?}} If the answer is ‘yesterday’, you are in good company, as chatbots are now part of everyday school life. {{The real question is whether}} they [[might]] be doing far too much of our thinking for us.

options.why: A direct question involves the readers, and the last sentence names the issue of the article.

options.label: Name the aims of the article
options.text: In this article I want to describe how AI tools can help students with their learning. I also want to explain the risks of relying on AI for schoolwork, and at the end I want to suggest rules for using AI in a way that supports learning.
options.reject: This copies the task word for word and uses ‘want to’ three times. Use your own words and a hook that makes people read on.
options.rejectDe: Die Inhaltspunkte sind wörtlich aus der Aufgabe übernommen, dazu dreimal „want to“. Eigene Worte und ein Hook sind gefragt.

steps.q: Body paragraph 1: how can AI tools help students with their learning?
steps.de: Erster Inhaltspunkt: wie KI-Werkzeuge beim Lernen helfen können. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then describe one way AI can help with learning and give an example of your own.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann eine Möglichkeit beschreiben, wie KI beim Lernen hilft, mit einem eigenen Beispiel.

options.label: Explanations on demand

map.partner: {{The clearest benefit of these tools is [[probably]]}} that explanations are available at any time. A chatbot does not get tired of the same question, and students who missed a point can ask for simpler words, a new example or a step-by-step solution. {{For shy learners, this [[may]] be}} the first time they dare to ask.
map.shortcut: {{Admittedly, the clearest benefit of these tools is [[probably]]}} that explanations are available at any time. A chatbot does not get tired of the same question, and students who missed a point can ask for simpler words, a new example or a step-by-step solution. {{For shy learners, this [[may]] be}} the first time they dare to ask.

options.why: The topic sentence names the benefit, and the examples show what it looks like in practice.

options.label: A private teacher
options.text: Many students use AI as a kind of private teacher. When I do not understand a topic, the chatbot can explain me the grammar or the maths again in simple words. It also gives useful informations for projects and controls my answers before a test, so I can see where I still have problems.
options.reject: Three typical mistakes: ‘explain me’ (→ explain … to me), ‘informations’ (→ information, no plural) and ‘controls my answers’ (→ checks my answers).
options.rejectDe: Drei typische Fehler: explain me → explain … to me, informations → information (kein Plural), controls → checks (false friend: „kontrollieren“).

options.label: Practice and feedback
options.text: {{AI tools can certainly help with practice and feedback.}} Before a test, some students ask for quiz questions and then for extra ones on whatever they got wrong. Others paste in a draft and get comments on structure and grammar within seconds. {{Such quick feedback [[tends to]] be most useful}} when students correct the mistakes themselves.
options.why: Two concrete uses, and the last sentence adds a careful comment on how to get the most out of them.

steps.de: Der Absatz geht weiter: ein Beispiel. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then add an example of your own: how could a student use AI to practise?
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann ein eigenes Beispiel ergänzen: Wie könnte jemand mit KI üben?

options.label: A student’s voice
options.text: {{When we asked around at school how students use chatbots,}} {NAME}, 17, gave a typical answer: “I ask the chatbot to quiz me, not to write for me. When it just hands me the solution, I forget it by the next day.” {{Experiences like this suggest that}} the way AI is used [[may]] matter more than the tool itself.
options.why: A quote makes the article lively, and the last sentence draws a careful conclusion from it.

options.label: Speaking practice
options.text: {{Language learning is a good example of this.}} A student preparing for an oral exam can hold a whole conversation in English with a chatbot, ask it to play an interviewer and get corrections afterwards. {{Unlike a classmate, a chatbot never laughs at mistakes,}} which [[seems to]] make many learners more willing to speak.
options.why: A concrete situation from school life that shows a use many readers have not thought of.

steps.q: Body paragraph 2: what are the risks of relying on AI for schoolwork?
steps.de: Zweiter Inhaltspunkt: die Risiken, wenn man sich beim Lernen und bei Hausübungen auf KI verlässt. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then explain the risk in your own words and say what it can lead to.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann das Risiko mit eigenen Worten erklären und sagen, wohin es führen kann.

options.label: The temptation to copy
options.text: {{Yet the biggest risk [[may well]] be copying.}} A summary of a novel or a finished essay is only a click away, and anyone who hands it in skips exactly the thinking that homework is meant to train. {{Such students [[are likely to]] struggle}} when no help is available: in a test or at the Matura.
options.why: The topic sentence names the risk, and the paragraph shows where it leads, using careful language.

options.label: Confident but wrong
options.text: {{There is a catch, though: chatbots sound just as confident when they are wrong.}} They produce text by predicting which words come next, not by checking facts, so they [[may]] mix up dates, get a calculation wrong or invent a source. {{Students who trust every answer [[are likely to]]}} learn mistakes as if they were facts.
options.why: It explains why chatbots make mistakes, which makes the warning convincing.

options.label: A clear warning
options.text: AI is the end of real learning. Every student who uses a chatbot is cheating, and the answers are always wrong anyway. Teachers can never find out what has been copied, so homework is now completely useless. Anyone who uses these tools will forget how to think for themselves.
options.reject: These are sweeping claims (every, always, never) that are simply not true. An honest article weighs the risks and uses careful language such as may, tend to or is likely to.
options.rejectDe: Pauschale Behauptungen (every, always, never) stimmen so nicht. Ein ehrlicher Artikel wägt ab und formuliert vorsichtig (may, tend to, is likely to).

steps.q: Which other risk do we add?
steps.de: Der Absatz geht weiter: ein weiteres Risiko. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then explain this risk in your own words and give a reason.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann das Risiko mit eigenen Worten erklären und begründen.

options.label: Learning without effort
options.text: {{A second, quieter risk is learning without effort.}} Memory research has long suggested that we remember things better when we have to work them out ourselves. {{When an app removes every difficulty,}} the knowledge [[might]] never stick, even if nobody has cheated.
options.why: It names a risk that has nothing to do with cheating, which makes the article more thoughtful.

options.label: Privacy
options.text: {{Privacy is another point to keep in mind.}} Many tools store what users type, and some use it to improve future versions. {{Personal details, photos of friends or}} other people’s work [[probably]] do not belong in a chatbot at all, however convenient it [[might]] seem.
options.why: It adds a practical risk that readers can avoid at once.

steps.q: Body paragraph 3: which rules help students to use AI in a way that supports learning?
steps.de: Dritter Inhaltspunkt: Regeln für einen Umgang mit KI, der das Lernen unterstützt. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then add your own rules and say why they help.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann eigene Regeln ergänzen und begründen.

options.label: Rules for good use
options.text: There are some simple rules for using AI well. Students should ask AI only for hints and explanations, not for complete answers. On the contrary, they should check important facts in a second source. Hence, it is a good idea to tell teachers when AI has helped with a piece of work, for example in a short note.
options.reject: The rules are good, but two linkers are wrong: ‘On the contrary’ does not add a second rule (→ In addition), and ‘Hence’ makes honesty sound like a result of checking facts (→ Finally).
options.rejectDe: Gute Regeln, falsche Linking words: On the contrary fügt nichts hinzu (→ In addition), Hence behauptet eine Folge, die es nicht gibt (→ Finally).

options.label: Three simple rules
options.text: {{Fortunately, a few simple rules can keep these problems in check.}} {{First, ask for}} explanations, hints and practice questions rather than finished answers. {{Second, check}} every important fact in a second source. {{Finally, be open about using a chatbot:}} a short note on how AI helped [[is likely to]] earn more trust than a suspiciously perfect text.
options.why: Clear order with First, Second and Finally, and the last rule is explained.

options.label: Treat it like a tutor
options.text: {{The best protection is to treat the chatbot like a tutor, not a ghostwriter.}} A good tutor asks questions and gives hints instead of solutions, and the chatbot can be told to do the same. {{It is equally wise to}} double-check facts and be open about using AI, as teachers [[tend to]] prefer honesty to excuses.
options.why: One clear picture (tutor, not ghostwriter) that readers will remember, plus honesty as a rule.

steps.de: Der Absatz geht weiter: ein weiterer Vorschlag. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then explain the idea in your own words and say why it works.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Idee mit eigenen Worten erklären und sagen, warum sie funktioniert.

options.label: A class agreement
options.text: {{Such rules work best when a whole class agrees on them.}} Some classes write their own AI agreement at the start of the year, stating what is allowed in homework, what is not and how help should be noted. {{Students who have helped to set such rules [[seem to]]}} take them more seriously, and teachers know what to expect.
options.why: It shows how rules can be agreed together, which makes them easier to follow.

options.label: Time without the tool
options.text: {{Rules aside, nothing replaces regular practice without any help.}} Writing a paragraph by hand, solving a problem on paper or summarising a chapter from memory shows what has really been learnt. {{After all, exams [[are unlikely to]]}} reward skills that were always left to a machine.
options.why: A practical tip with a convincing reason: exams test what we can do ourselves.

steps.q: How do we end the article?
steps.de: Der Schluss rundet den Artikel ab, passend zur gewählten Grundhaltung. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then sum up the article’s view in one or two sentences of your own.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Sicht des Artikels in ein bis zwei eigenen Sätzen zusammenfassen.

options.label: Sum up the view

map.partner: {{All in all, AI is neither a miracle nor a monster.}} Its help is real and so are its risks, but with a few clear rules, it [[may]] well become the best study partner our generation has had.
map.shortcut: {{All in all, AI is neither a miracle nor a monster.}} It can help, but the temptation to let it think for us is real, and most of us [[might]] give in more often than we admit. So follow clear rules and keep the hard work for yourself.

options.why: A balanced first sentence, then a short look back at help, risks and rules that fits our view.

options.label: Leave readers with a question

map.partner: {{So next time you open a chatbot, ask yourself one question:}} am I using it to learn or to avoid learning? {{If the honest answer is ‘to learn’}} and you keep to the rules, you [[may]] have found the best study partner there is.
map.shortcut: {{So next time you open a chatbot, ask yourself one question:}} am I using it to learn or to avoid learning? {{If the honest answer is ‘to avoid it’,}} no rule will help, and closing the app [[might]] be the smartest decision of the day.

options.why: It speaks to the readers directly, sums up the article in one question and leaves them with something to think about.

steps.q: Now that the article is finished, which title do we choose?
steps.de: Zuletzt wählen wir den Titel für unseren Artikel.
steps.own: Short and catchy: a question, a slogan or a play on words that fits our article.
steps.ownDe: Kurz und packend: eine Frage, ein Slogan oder ein Wortspiel, passend zu unserem Artikel.

options.label: Three short verbs
options.why: Three short verbs show the risk at once and make readers curious.

options.label: A slogan for our view
options.why: A short slogan that already contains the message of our article.

options.label: A play on words
options.text: Help, hack or habit? Learning with AI
options.why: Three words with the same first sound make the title easy to remember.

checks.en: A catchy title that fits our view
An introduction that makes readers curious and leads to the question
All three content points: how AI helps, the risks, rules for good use
Five paragraphs; each body paragraph opens with a topic sentence linked to what came before
Careful claims: hedging with may, might, tend to or is likely to instead of always and never
Readers are drawn in by a scene, a question or direct address; neutral register, no slang
The conclusion adds no new arguments

teacher.aim: Die Klasse baut gemeinsam einen Artikel nach SRDP-Standard über KI beim Lernen: ehrlich über den Nutzen (Erklärungen, Übung, Feedback) und die Risiken (Abschreiben, falsche Antworten), mit Regeln und dem Gedanken, die eigene KI-Nutzung offenzulegen. Fokus: Hedging – vorsichtige Aussagen mit may, might, tend to, be likely to, seem to und probably.
teacher.prep: A/B/C/D-Karten austeilen, eine Garnitur pro Person (ohne Karten: 1–4 Finger, die Tasten 1–4 wählen wie A–D). Beamer im Vollbild. Die Aufgabe am Beamer enthält alles Nötige. Im Gerüst-Modus den eingebauten Timer nutzen: 5–6 min pro Absatz.
teacher.heft: Neue Seite: Datum (rechts), „Article“ als Überschrift, darunter 2 Zeilen für den Titel frei lassen (der Titel kommt zuletzt). Jeder Absatz beginnt nach einer Leerzeile, am Rand stehen die Randwörter Intro, Body 1, Body 2, Body 3 und Conclusion. Hedging-Ausdrücke grün unterstreichen.
teacher.flow: Volltext kurz (50 min): 3 min Aufgabe lesen und Grundhaltung wählen, 6 weitere Entscheidungen à ca. 2 min, Abschreiben ca. 25 min, 5 min Checkliste. Volltext lang (100 min): zusätzlich drei Fortsetzungen, die Body 1, 2 und 3 verlängern (kein neuer Absatz), Abschreiben ca. 40 min, am Ende Wortzahl und Hedging-Ausdrücke zählen. Gerüst kurz (60 min): 3 min Aufgabe und Grundhaltung, pro Absatz 1 min Entscheidung, 5–6 min eigenes Schreiben, 1 min Vergleich mit dem Modell; am Ende 2 min Titel und 4 min Checkliste. In 50 Minuten: Schluss und Titel als Hausübung. Gerüst lang (100 min): dieselben Phasen für die fünf Absätze, dazu drei Fortsetzungen à ca. 6 min (1 min Entscheidung, 4 min Schreiben im selben Absatz, 1 min Vergleich).
teacher.traps: Introduction C (LSR): Inhaltspunkte wörtlich aus der Aufgabe, dreimal „I want to“. Body 1 B (LSA): explain me, informations, controls my answers (statt checks). Body 2 C (TA): Pauschalurteile mit every, always, never statt ehrlicher Abwägung – genau das Gegenteil von Hedging. Body 3 A (CC): On the contrary statt In addition, Hence ohne Ursache. Kürzel: TA = Erfüllung der Aufgabenstellung, CC = Kohärenz und Kohäsion, LSR = Spektrum sprachlicher Mittel, LSA = Sprachrichtigkeit.
teacher.notes: Der Artikel hat in beiden Längen fünf Absätze (Intro, drei Hauptteile, Schluss); die lange Fassung macht Body 1, 2 und 3 mit je einer Fortsetzung länger, ohne neue Absätze. Keine Produkt- oder Firmennamen verwenden; es geht um KI-Werkzeuge allgemein. Die Grundhaltung im ersten Schritt steuert Einstieg, Schluss und Titel B; beide Haltungen sind ausgewogen, Nutzen und Risiken kommen in jeder Fassung vor. Sachinfo: Chatbots erzeugen Text, indem sie wahrscheinliche Fortsetzungen berechnen, nicht indem sie Fakten prüfen; daher sind falsche Daten, Rechenfehler und erfundene Quellen möglich. Die Gedächtnisforschung zeigt seit Langem, dass selbst Erarbeitetes besser behalten wird. Gesprächsanlass: Wie wird an eurer Schule KI-Hilfe offengelegt? Die Schüler:innen nicht nach eigenen Regelverstößen fragen. Für die Namenslücke (Fortsetzung von Body 1, Option A) nur erfundene Vornamen, keine Namen von Mitschüler:innen oder Lehrer:innen. Differenzierung: Schnelle ergänzen im Gerüst-Modus pro Absatz einen Satz mit einem weiteren Hedging-Ausdruck (appear to, perhaps). Hausübung: zweite Fassung mit der anderen Grundhaltung.
